children: The Philippine central bank expects inflation to remain elevated in October, driven by higher domestic fuel, electricity and transport costs. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas expects this to be partly offset by lower prices of key agricultural commodities, including rice, vegetables, meat, and fish amid favorable supply conditions. The central bank said it will continue to assess the impact of the latest Middle East developments on the Philippine inflation and economic outlook. The BSP projects inflation to settle between 7.1% and 8.1% for October, compared with 7.2% in September. The October data are due next week.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
